_comment: DELIVERY-GATE-1 fix manifest, read by scripts/check-delivery.py.
EVERY FIELD HERE IS A CLAIM THAT THE CHECKER VERIFIES AGAINST A PRIMARY
SOURCE. Nothing in this file is trusted. A commit that does not exist, a
gate that is not in RendererFeatureRegistry.h, an `expect_default` that
disagrees with the C++ reader, a `needle` that is absent from the named
path at the named commit -- each of those is an INTEGRITY FAILURE (exit 2),
not a skipped entry. That is the whole point: this manifest is the kind of
artifact that historically became the lie, so it is the artifact under the
most suspicion.
FIELDS
id             stable name, used as --fix argument
commit         the commit that INTRODUCED the code (git log -S on the reader)
gate           MC2_* env var, or null for an ungated change
expect_default 'ON' | 'OFF' | a decimal string for numeric gates | null
exe_needle     a literal the fix puts in the IMAGE (uniform name, gate
name). Strongest evidence tier: it is read out of the
binary's own bytes, so a revert, a failed compile or a
stale copy cannot fake it.
code_evidence  [{path, needle, alternate_paths?}] checked against the embedded commit;
alternate_paths names audited relocations after a source split.
Each evidence item must match at least one path at that commit.
The original path is still checked at the introducing commit.
Per-install source checks catch WITHDRAWN code, which ancestry
alone cannot (a revert leaves the introducing commit an
ancestor forever).
data           [{kind, path|glob, needle?, min_count?}] the deploy-tree
files the fix needs. kind=file with a needle is the
half-data shape: the file is there but predates the fix, so
glGetUniformLocation returns -1 and the gate runs OFF while
reporting ON.

fixes.note: VEHICLE-NIGHT-LIT-1. Introduced default-OFF, promoted to default-ON by VEHICLE-LIGHTING-PATH-1. The per-install default column is therefore expected to DIFFER between installs, which is exactly the thing this tool exists to show.

The half-data fix named in its own commit message: 'the deployed shaders/ tree must carry the new gos_tex_vertex_lighted.vert or the uniform does not exist in the program, glGetUniformLocation returns -1, the set silently no-ops and the gate runs OFF while reporting ON.'

The vehicle light gather. GVAppearance called neither CacheGpuLightData() nor the batcher, so every vehicle rendered with numLights_==0, calc_light took its early-return and returned vec3(1,1,1) -- raw albedo, unlit, day AND night. This is one of the fixes that answers the user's own 'the vehicles look wrong' report, so its delivery is the question, not its correctness. HALF-DATA SHAPE: the commit also adds the night light-pool term to gos_tex_vertex_lighted.frag; a deploy tree carrying the OLD frag has no calcLightPools, the pool contribution silently vanishes, and the gate reports ON.

Separate entry from VEHICLE-LIT-PATH-1 ON PURPOSE, because the two have different delivery: an install can carry the gather call and NOT this follow-up, in which case only the first SHAPE_NODE leaf gets a light row and every other leaf still renders at raw albedo. Its own commit message records that with only CacheGpuLightData(), deterministic A/B poses showed ZERO pixel change -- i.e. the first fix alone was user-invisible. exe_needle is null deliberately: the fix adds no new string literal, so the binary tier cannot speak and source@sha is the strongest available evidence. That is a weaker answer, and it is reported as such rather than upgraded. Split 6532c1ca9 moved the unchanged call to gvactor_render.cpp; both source locations are accepted, with the declaration and call still required at the embedded commit.

The concrete overlay-cement adopt: the delivered cure for 'the concrete is a patchwork / the transition tiles are the wrong colour'. COMMIT IS 3ab322a0, THE INTRODUCER, NOT a8ea9be5, THE MERGE, and the difference was found by this manifest overstating it. Named against the merge, every install built between 08:33 and the merge reported EVIDENCE TIERS DISAGREE (binary=YES source@sha=YES ancestry=NO): the needles are satisfied by the 08:33 introduction, so the entry graded 'delivered' on binaries that predate the merge. Pointing it at the introducer makes the 6/18 mean exactly what it says -- these installs carry the adopt path as first shipped. What the merge ADDED (the widening to all 17 overlay ids, and the runway superset guard) is graded separately by OVERLAY-CEMENT-ARTGUARD-2, whose exe_needle is unique to that afternoon work and which answers 0/18. Two entries, because they have two different delivery answers. HALF-DATA: the whole repaint is computed in terrain_overlay.frag behind u_overlayCementAdopt; a deploy tree with the old frag ignores the uniform and the tile colours are unchanged while the gate reports ON.

The TileIsRoadArt runway superset guard. Adds NO gate of its own; it runs inside `if (OverlayCementAdoptEnabled() && Terrain::mapData)` (gos_terrain_indirect.cpp:1826), so MC2_OVERLAY_CEMENT_ADOPT is genuinely its gate and is recorded as such rather than left null -- a null would have graded the default axis an unconditional YES and claimed delivery on an install where the adopt gate is off. exe_needle is a printf format literal unique to this commit, so the binary tier can answer even though the fix adds no uniform.

Albedo-scaled daylight terrain ambient floor. Commit is 96ffc35d, the INTRODUCER (12:43), not ea7ef347, the merge onto canonical (13:35) -- same correction as OVERLAY-CEMENT-ADOPT-1, applied before it could overstate anything. It does not change this entry's answer (both are after the newest binary on this disk, so it is 0/18 either way), which is exactly why it was worth fixing while the answer was not in dispute. A FLOAT gate: the reader is `if (!e || !e[0]) return 0.35f;`, which every numeric rule in check-delivery.py missed until DELIVERY-CLOSE-1 -- the rules hard-coded the pointer name `v` and matched integers only, so this gate classified UNKNOWN and could not grade as delivered on any install no matter what it contained. expect_default is the literal 0.35, not 'ON', so a rewrite that changed the shipped strength while keeping it nonzero is caught.

A RETRACTION, not a feature: CONCRETE-DELIVER-2 reverts a default-ON that the promoting lane's own status doc had already retracted in writing. A numeric gate, so check-gate-default-agreement.py skips it as 'value-read (not a boolean gate)' -- nothing else in the tree compares its per-install default against the tip. Grading concrete on an install that predates this commit grades WITHDRAWN code.

Default-ON and degrades to a silent no-op when the .beauty sidecar is absent (check-beauty-sidecars.py module docstring). scripts/deploy_payload.py deliberately never walks data/missions/*.beauty/, so the sidecar reaches a tree only by a manual copy.
